Subject: Bancorp: Redwood eval plan and next steps

Hi Samantha & Tom,

Great to meet you both on the call today—quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get a customer-specific eval running on Redwood. High-level goals we heard:
- Primary: Retrieval-augmented summarization and Q&A over internal policy docs (reduce time-to-answer, minimize hallucinations)
- Secondary: Short-form email draft assistance for relationship managers

Success criteria you mentioned: 95th percentile latency < 300ms, factuality/hallucination rate < 5% on core Q&A, and slot extraction accuracy > 85%. Correct me if I mis-stated.

What we recommend for an initial eval (so we can give numbers and model recommendations):
1) Dataset: 300-500 representative examples covering RAG queries + edge cases (PII redacted). CSV with columns: id, prompt, ground_truth, intent_tag, notes. (I attached a blank prompt set template: bancorp_eval_promptset.csv)
2) Models to benchmark: Llama-2-13B-chat (quantized) and Mistral-7B-instruct (as a faster baseline). We'll also surface a smaller 4-8B model if you want cost-first options.
3) Run config: deterministic decoding (temp 0.0-0.2) for eval, max_tokens 512, top_p 0.95, batch size ~8. Our SEs will tune quantization and batching to balance latency/cost.
4) Scoring: token-level F1 for extraction tasks, exact-match + fuzzy string match for QA, plus a small human review sample for hallucination/factuality.

Next steps / asks from your side:
- Share a sample CSV (300 examples is fine initially; 100 is ok to start) and any internal scoring rubric you have.
- Let us know if this must run in a VPC/on-prem environment for data residency or compliance.
- Preferred timeline for results (we can usually run a first pass within 48-72 hours after we have the dataset).

I'll loop in Dev (SE) to share the eval-run instructions and to propose a run config.

Thanks,

Hi all — quick technical note on dataset format and the eval run config we recommend for a clean comparison.

Required CSV format (columns): id, prompt, ground_truth, context_doc_id (optional), split (train/val/test), notes
- id: unique per example
- prompt: full prompt as sent to model (include retrieval context placeholders if used)
- ground_truth: expected output string (for extraction, canonicalized form is best)

Scoring: we run the following out-of-the-box in the Redwood eval harness:
- Exact match rate (for canonical extraction fields)
- Token-level F1 (for partial matches)
- BLEU/ROUGE for summarization when applicable
- Hallucination flag: automatic heuristics + manual spot-check (10-20 examples)

Models & config to benchmark (initial pass):
- redwood/llama2-13b-chat-q4 (quantized 13B chat variant) — expected best quality/latency tradeoff
- redwood/mistral-7b-instruct-q4 — faster baseline, lower cost
- Optionally run a 4-8B model (gptj-6b-equivalent) if cost constrained

Runtime params we suggest for eval: temperature=0.0, top_p=0.95, max_tokens=512, stop sequences as needed. Use deterministic seeds for sampling-based metrics. For throughput, batch_size=8 (tune up if latency SLO allows).

How we run it on Redwood:
- Hosted (quick): upload CSV to temporary S3 link and create an eval job in Redwood Console (we'll do this for a first-pass).
- Private/VPC: we can run the evaluator inside your VPC with direct S3 access and zero data egress — requires a short config step (we'll share an infra checklist).

I'll attach a short instructions PDF (redwood_eval_instructions.pdf) that has the CLI snippet and an example evaluation job payload. If you want, we can run the first job internally and share the results + a short walkthrough.

Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Adding a quick note on thresholds and monitoring. Good plan all around. Proposed gating logic we typically use:
- Primary metric: extraction exact-match or token-F1 (define per field). If primary metric < 0.82 on validation set -> block rollout.
- Hallucination alert: if automated hallucination flag > 5% -> require human review sample before any rollout.
- Regression monitoring: tie these eval results to a Redwood Console alert (we can create a regression alert that monitors the same test set on every model rollout).

Dev — can you create the initial eval job in our sandbox account and share the job id? I'll set up an alert and hook the job to the deal in HubSpot.
